text:
Anna: Heads-up — noticed a steady stream of customer reports that quota dashboards are double-counting for some requests after yesterday's routing header rollout. Customers see spikes but backend traces show single requests.
Josh: Ugh. Any repro or a specific tenant affected?
Anna: Yep — tenant `acme-inc` is a clear repro. I grabbed a curl trace. Looks like we set `X-Policy: reserved` on the client side but the metering service is seeing both `x-policy` and `x-policy-legacy`.
Anna: ```
> curl -v -H "X-Policy: reserved" https://api.redwood-inference/v1/generate
< Request forwarded with headers: x-policy: reserved, x-policy-legacy: reserved
```
Anna: We never intended to emit `x-policy-legacy` from the client, but it's appearing in production traffic.
Priya: Interesting — SDK note: recent HTTP client upgrade in TS/py added automatic header normalization for camelCase/legacy compat. If the runtime adds a `x-meter-mode` header, our client lib has code that maps unknown headers into a legacy keyset for older proxies.
Priya: In other words, SDKs may be duping the header to support old proxies. We didn't think that would hit metering.
Marco: On the runtime side we rolled a small change that adds `X-Meter-Mode: aggregate` as a sibling header for internal routing experiments. Looks like the SDK header normalizer treats `X-Meter-Mode` and `x-meter-mode` separately and emits a `x-meter-mode-legacy`.
Lena: So combination of runtime and SDK behavior -> two headers reaching the metering pipeline -> double billing?
Anna: Exactly. Console shows 2x token-metered for same request hash.
Josh: We need a quick mitigation. Options: (1) server-side shim that collapses duplicate policy/meter headers, (2) patch SDKs to stop emitting legacy passthrough, (3) console-side dedupe heuristic.
Priya: Patch timeline: TS/py can get a patch release today if we keep it opt-in env flag. Go is trickier due to exported API changes — might be a minor breaking bump and would take longer.
Priya: Proposed quick client fix (TS/py): add env `REDWOOD_LEGACY_HEADER_PASSTHROUGH=false` defaulting to true for a day then flip via release. Patch is ~8 LOC.
Marco: I can deploy a server-side header-collapser in the edge router as a emergency rule to de-dup `x-policy*` and `x-meter-mode*`. That buys time.
Anna: Can we also emit a telemetry event when duplicate policy headers are present so we can count affected SDK versions?
console-bot: New alert created: metering.duplicate-headers detected for tenant acme-inc (rule: header-dup-2026-03).
Josh: Good. Priya — can you prepare the patch and a quick changelog blurb for the py/ts releases? Also include a small telemetry ping so console can show impacted installs.
Priya: On it. I'll include a minimal telemetry field: `dup_header_detected: true` when we observe both original+legacy being generated client-side. Will gate behind env flag.
Lena: For UX: Console should show an annotation on quota dashboard when dedupe is active and show affected SDK versions. Product wants a customer-facing note too.
Anna: Quick action list:
- Marco: deploy header-collapser rule to edge (ASAP) — owner: Marco — ETA 1h.
- Priya: TS/py patch + telemetry opt-in flag & release today — owner: Priya — ETA 4h.
- Josh: Add console dedupe visualization + small alert linking to incident note — owner: Josh — ETA EOD.
- Anna: Draft customer note for affected tenants and post to #customer-success — owner: Anna — ETA 2h.
Josh: Also: schedule a short postmortem to decide long-term: keep shim, change SDK normalization, or change runtime header strategy.
Priya: Confirmed repro steps and will open PRs linking to this thread.
Anna: Thanks. If anyone sees additional tenants in console, ping me and tag the thread. :thumbsup:
Marco: Header-collapser live on edge (rolled back a bad rule once), now stable. Logs show dup headers dropped for ~120 requests — working.
Priya: TS patch published `@redwood/sdk@2.14.1` with `REDWOOD_LEGACY_HEADER_PASSTHROUGH=false` env and telemetry opt-in. Py patch `redwood==1.9.3` published.
console-bot: Telemetry event: dup_header_detected=12 for versions ["ts-2.14.0","py-1.9.2"].
Anna: Great progress. We'll keep the edge rule for 24h and revert after SDK uptake. Follow-up postmortem next week.
